hooks.line: My whole crew knew my wife was cheating for two years. Nobody told me. When I found out why they stayed quiet, it broke me worse than she did.
hooks.card: none
hooks.scroll: Sunny backyard party, medium shot, front, eye level, static: the man in the teal-and-orange floral shirt holds a plate of food, smiles, then the smile drops into confusion while the circle mingles behind him under the bunting.
hooks.thumb: the source's first frame: the man at the buffet table, plate in hand, smile breaking to confusion, guests behind him; no words beyond the running caption.

hooks.line: My father had been in the ground six hours when my cousin pulled me aside. Everybody been knowing about my wife and my best friend. Everybody but me.
hooks.card: running caption only, first chunk: "My father had been"
hooks.scroll: Funeral reception, marble floor, soft window light: mid-handshake with a mourner, a hand grabs the man's black suit sleeve and pulls him out of the line, the paper cup in his other hand sloshing over.
hooks.thumb: the man in his black suit, his cousin's mouth at his ear, his eyes fixed past her on a couple standing close across the hall; words "AT MY FATHER'S FUNERAL"

hooks.line: Thanksgiving, my house. I carved the turkey and smiled the whole meal. I'd already seen his hand on her back through the kitchen glass. The whole circle knew before me.
hooks.card: running caption only, first chunk: "Thanksgiving, my house."
hooks.scroll: Thanksgiving table, warm evening light: the carving knife sinks into the turkey on the first word while he holds a wide, fixed smile; over his shoulder, soft through the frosted kitchen door, a man's hand slides down a woman's back.
hooks.thumb: wide from the far end of the table, the man standing at the head with the knife over the turkey, every face at the table turned toward him smiling; words "SMILED THE WHOLE MEAL"

hooks.line: End of the night, I drove him home like we were still best friends. He'd been with my wife two years. Whole crew been knowing.
hooks.card: running caption only, first chunk: "End of the night,"
hooks.scroll: Night, car interior, streetlights strobing across two faces: the passenger throws his head back laughing; the driver's knuckles tighten white on the wheel and his eyes never leave the road.
hooks.thumb: two-shot through the windshield at night, the passenger mid-laugh, the driver stone-faced with a streetlight across his eyes; words "I DROVE HIM HOME"

hooks.take: the friend's excuse at the diner
hooks.line: One of the guys finally told me straight up. Two years they didn't know how to tell me about my wife. Said I seemed cool with it. I wasn't cool with it. I was just invisible.
hooks.card: running caption only, first chunk: "One of the guys"
hooks.scroll: Diner booth, warm light: the friend across the table says it and looks away; the man's coffee cup stops an inch from his lips, and he sets it down without drinking.
hooks.thumb: the man alone in the diner booth, the seat across from him empty, his coffee untouched; words "THEY SAID I SEEMED COOL WITH IT"

hooks.line: Every two weeks, same chair, fresh cut, laughing with the whole shop. Two years of that. The whole circle been knowing about my wife. Nobody told me.
hooks.card: running caption only, first chunk: "Every two weeks, same chair,"
hooks.scroll: Barbershop, afternoon light: the barber whips the cape off and spins the chair to face the mirror; the man grins at his fresh cut, and in the mirror two men from the circle on the waiting bench trade a look and go quiet. No blade in frame; the camera stays on his face and the mirror, never on his neck.
hooks.thumb: the barbershop mirror: his grin up front, the two men on the bench behind him looking away; words "FRESH CUT. LAST TO KNOW."

hooks.line: My whole crew knew my wife was cheating for two years. Nobody told me. When I found out why they stayed quiet, it broke me worse than she did.

hooks.take: Thanksgiving: he made a toast anyway
hooks.line: I watched my best friend put his hand on my wife's back in my own kitchen. Then I carved the turkey like nothing happened. Made a toast.
hooks.card: I CARVED THE TURKEY / LIKE NOTHING HAPPENED
hooks.scroll: Close-up of a carving knife sinking into a roast turkey. Focus racks past the blade to the glass kitchen door behind, where a man's hand slides onto a woman's back.
hooks.thumb: The protagonist at the head of the Thanksgiving table with his glass raised mid-toast, smiling, eyes wet. Deshawn and Alicia sit side by side at the far end. Words: "I MADE A TOAST."

hooks.line: My father had been in the ground six hours when my cousin pulled me aside. Man, I'm sorry, but everyone's been knowing.
hooks.card: SIX HOURS AFTER / MY FATHER'S FUNERAL
hooks.scroll: A funeral reception hall with gold chairs and white roses. The protagonist, in a black suit, is mid-handshake in the receiving line when a woman's hand grips his arm and pulls him out of it.
hooks.thumb: The protagonist's face in a black suit and tie, white roses behind him, the cousin's mouth at his ear. Words: "EVERYONE'S BEEN KNOWING."

hooks.line: She said she was going to yoga. She was going to a hotel. Two years, and the whole circle knew.

hooks.thumb: A rolled yoga mat on a hotel bed, a key card on top. Words: "SHE SAID YOGA."

hooks.line: If you're noticing your razor bumps slowly getting worse, your face wash might be cleaning your face, but doing absolutely nothing as to why they keep coming back.
hooks.card: How do I stop razor bumps?
hooks.scroll: Propped phone, front camera, medium close-up at eye level: he sits centred at his desk under the blue LED strip, tilts his chin up and runs two fingers along the razor bumps on the side of his neck to show them, the card near the top of frame.
hooks.thumb: The source's first frame, held: him mid-gesture with two fingers on the bumps along his neck, eyes on the lens, "How do I stop razor bumps?" in bold white at the top.

hooks.take: right after the shave, one swipe
hooks.line: One swipe and the razor bumps are already starting. The hair is growing right back into your skin, and your face wash never gets there.
hooks.card: One swipe. / Razor bumps already.
hooks.scroll: At the desk under the blue LED, he drags a razor once down the side of his neck toward the lens, lowers it, and tilts his chin so the line of red bumps along that one stroke faces the camera.
hooks.thumb: The razor frozen mid-stroke on his neck, a line of red bumps just behind the blade, his eyes on the lens; "ONE SWIPE." in bold white top centre.

hooks.take: two days after a clean shave
hooks.line: You can shave your neck clean and a day or two later it looks like this again. Razor bumps, right back, and your face wash never touched why.
hooks.card: Shaved clean. / 2 days later.
hooks.scroll: He runs the backs of his fingers slowly up his neck against the grain, they catch on the bumps, and he stops and holds on the roughest patch under his jaw.
hooks.thumb: A tight crop of his knuckles stopped on a patch of razor bumps and dark marks under the jaw, with the crewneck collar and silver chain in frame; "2 DAYS AFTER THE SHAVE" in bold white.

hooks.line: If you keep pulling your shirt up so nobody sees the razor bumps, your face wash never got to why they're there.
hooks.card: Still hiding / the razor bumps?
hooks.scroll: He grabs the neckline of his grey crewneck with both hands and pulls it up over his neck to his chin, holds it, then lets it drop so the bumps and dark marks show.
hooks.thumb: Both hands holding the crewneck up to his chin, only his eyes and a strip of bumped jaw above it, looking into the lens; "STILL HIDING IT?" in bold white.

hooks.take: tried every razor, late at night after a bad shave
hooks.line: Five blade, single blade, rotary, foil. Makes no difference. The razor bumps still come back, because none of them reach the hair already under my skin.
hooks.card: Every razor. / Same razor bumps.
hooks.scroll: After dark, the room lit only by the blue LED and his front light, he sets four razors on the desk one after another, slaps the last one down, and points straight at the bumps on his neck.
hooks.thumb: Four razors in a row on the desk in the blue light, him behind them pointing at his neck; "TRIED EVERY RAZOR" in bold white.

hooks.line: Same spot, every single time you shave. The razor bumps come back right where they were, and washing with your hands never gets under there.
hooks.card: Same spot. / Every shave.
hooks.scroll: With one fingertip he traces a small circle around one patch of bumps and dark marks under his jaw, then taps the middle of it three times, eyes on the lens.
hooks.thumb: An extreme close-up of a fingertip circling one patch of razor bumps and dark marks under the jaw; "THE SAME SPOT. EVERY TIME." in bold white.

hooks.line: You can turn away, but I will never hide my face.
hooks.card: 2025 / how sad could it be...
